intro:
You are answering Modules One and Two. This paper exists so that nothing is hidden from you: it holds the one past question that has no part on your two modules, and below it a map of every part skipped in the other two papers.

Two reasons to spend twenty minutes here anyway: the objective half of your paper draws on all three modules, and if one of your two written questions turns out worse than you hoped, Question 3 is the fallback.

lockin.big: "Skipped is not the same as unknown. You know what you left out, and where its answer is."
lockin.sub: Module Three is objects, class diagrams and the behavioural diagrams. Design and acquisition sit outside your format entirely.

questions.heading: 2025/2026, Question Four: Vought Industries and the pharmaceutical system

scenario.text: Vought Industries have decided to acquire a Pharmaceutical Information System; the time frame is short and the project skills are not strategic a. What System Acquisition Strategy fits these requirements? Enumerate (3) other factors that support your choice. (3 mks) b. Mention any two (2) software architectural functions that Vought Industries will need in order to make the system perform properly. (3 mks) c. The choice of hardware architecture depends on four (4) nonfunctional requirements, the first is operational requirements, enumerate any other two types of hardware requirements. (3 mks) d. Interface design is the process of defining how the system will interact with external entities. Outline any three (3) principles of Interface design. (3 mks) e. Design and populate a Relational Database consisting of Customer, Order and Payment Type for the Pharmaceutical System (use dummy names and values and ensure to include primary keys for all unique IDs. You should have a minimum of 3 columns and 5 rows) (5.5 mks)

breakdown.question: What is this question actually asking, what have you been given, and what do the marks tell you about how much to write? Decide, then check.
breakdown.answer:
Given A firm buying a system, under time pressure, with no strategic in-house skills. Those two clues decide part a.

Asked The acquisition strategy and four short parts from Module Six Unit 1, then a small database to design and populate.

Watch "Short time frame" and "skills not strategic" both point away from building. Part e wants real dummy rows, not a description: draw the tables.

exam.problem: Write your answer to PQ 25/26 Q4 in your book first, one clear point for every mark. Then open the model answer and mark yourself against it.
exam.answer:
Answer · PQ 25/26 Q4

a. Acquisition strategy (3 marks)

Because the time frame is short and the skills are not strategic, buy a packaged (off-the-shelf) solution, or outsource, rather than build in-house. Supporting factors: the time available (buying is fastest); the in-house skills (they are lacking); and how strategic the system is (it is not core, so a package is fine); also cost and how well available packages fit the need.

b. Two software architectural functions (3 marks)

Any two of: data storage, data access logic, application (business) logic, and presentation logic.

c. Two more hardware non-functional requirements (3 marks)

Besides operational requirements: performance requirements and security requirements (the fourth is cultural and political requirements).

d. Three interface design principles (3 marks)

Consistency (the same action works the same way everywhere); simplicity and clarity (show only what is needed); and user feedback (the system confirms actions and reports errors clearly).

frames.teach: You are not preparing this question, so four frames only, for the fallback case. Every part of it belongs to the design and acquisition material, and the shape of each answer is a short list tied to the scenario.
frames.ask: The scenario says the time frame is short and the project skills are not strategic. What does that combination point at?

frames.check: Buying a package rather than building it, or outsourcing.
frames.teach: That is the whole of part (a): a short schedule and skills that are not core to the business point at purchasing a packaged solution, with customisation. Supporting factors: the requirements are common to the industry, the cost and timeline are predictable, and the vendor carries the maintenance.
frames.ask: Part (d) asks for three principles of interface design. Guess any two.

frames.check: Consistency, and clear feedback to the user.
frames.teach: The usual list: layout consistency, content awareness so the user always knows where they are, aesthetics, user experience matched to who the users are, consistency across screens, and minimal user effort, no more than three clicks to anything.
frames.ask: Part (e) asks you to design and populate a relational database. What earns the marks, beyond the table itself?

frames.check: The primary keys, and the foreign key that joins the tables.
frames.teach: Three tables, Customer, Order and Payment Type, each with at least three columns and five rows of plausible dummy data, every identifier marked as the primary key, and Order carrying the customer and payment type ids as foreign keys. Draw it as three small tables, not as prose.
